t2m.name: Air temperature (2 m)
t2m.definition: How warm the air is about 2 m above the ground.
t2m.citation: GMAO (2015), MERRA-2 tavgM_2d_slv_Nx V5.12.4, GES DISC, doi:10.5067/AP1B0BA5PD2K

precip.name: Precipitation
precip.definition: How much rain falls, in millimetres.
precip.citation: Huffman et al. (2023), GPM IMERG Final Precipitation L3 1 month 0.1° V07, GES DISC, doi:10.5067/GPM/IMERG/3B-MONTH/07

soil_moisture.name: Soil moisture (top 10 cm)
soil_moisture.definition: How much of the top 10 cm of soil is water (m³ of water per m³ of soil).
soil_moisture.source: FLDAS Noah land model (NASA, GLDAS family)
soil_moisture.citation: McNally (2018), FLDAS Noah Land Surface Model L4 Global Monthly 0.1° (MERRA-2 and CHIRPS), GES DISC, doi:10.5067/5NHC22T9375G

water_vapor.name: Water vapor (whole air column)
water_vapor.definition: All the water vapor in the air above a spot, as mm of water if it all fell as rain.
water_vapor.citation: AIRS project (2019), Aqua/AIRS L3 Monthly Standard Physical Retrieval 1° V7.0, GES DISC, doi:10.5067/UBENJB9D3T2H

no2.name: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2)
no2.definition: A polluting gas from car exhaust, power plants and factories, measured in the lower air.
no2.citation: Krotkov et al. (2019), OMI/Aura NO2 Cloud-Screened Tropospheric Column L3 Global 0.25° V3 (OMNO2d), GES DISC, doi:10.5067/Aura/OMI/DATA3007

ndvi.name: Vegetation greenness (NDVI)
ndvi.definition: How green and dense plants are, from -1 to 1: bare desert is about 0.1, dense crops are above 0.6.
ndvi.source: MODIS Terra MOD13A3 v061 (NASA LP DAAC, via AppEEARS)
ndvi.citation: Didan (2021), MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices Monthly L3 Global 1km SIN Grid V061, LP DAAC, doi:10.5067/MODIS/MOD13A3.061

method.series: Monthly area averages; seasonal cycle removed by subtracting each calendar month's mean; trend tests run on annual means of the monthly anomalies.
method.tests: Mann-Kendall (Kendall's tau vs. time) and OLS t-test, both two-sided at alpha = 0.05. Rate of change = Sen's slope with 95% CI.
method.verdict: significant = both tests p < 0.05; weak_evidence = only one; no_evidence = neither; too_short = fewer than 10 full years.
method.years_needed: Weatherhead et al. (1998): n* = [3.3*sigma_N/|w0| * sqrt((1+phi)/(1-phi))]^(2/3), sigma_N and phi from detrended monthly anomalies; 90% detection probability at 5% level.
method.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate across all series (q = 0.05).
references: Weatherhead et al. (1998) J. Geophys. Res. 103(D14):17149-17161, doi:10.1029/98JD00995
Benjamini & Hochberg (1995) J. R. Stat. Soc. B 57:289-300

series.summary: Precipitation over Amazon (Rondônia) is falling by about 273 mm/year, about 16% of its average level, per decade (1998–2024). This trend is statistically significant (p < 0.001): it is very unlikely to be chance.

Soil moisture (top 10 cm) over Amazon (Rondônia) is falling by about 0.0037 m³/m³, about 1% of its average level, per decade (1982–2025). This trend is statistically significant (p = 0.006): it is very unlikely to be chance.
Air temperature (2 m) over Amazon (Rondônia) is rising by about 0.5 °C per decade (1980–2025). This trend is statistically significant (p < 0.001): it is very unlikely to be chance.

Water vapor (whole air column) over Amazon (Rondônia) shows no clear trend (2003–2025). The estimated change of 0.27 mm per decade could be chance (p = 0.530). If it kept going at this rate, about 44 years of data would be needed to detect it; we have 23.

Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) over Greater Cairo is rising by about 0.37 ×10^15 molecules/cm², about 7% of its average level, per decade (2005–2025). This trend is statistically significant (p = 0.002): it is very unlikely to be chance.
Air temperature (2 m) over Greater Cairo is rising by about 0.31 °C per decade (1980–2025). This trend is statistically significant (p < 0.001): it is very unlikely to be chance.
